title: Memory Is Communication: The Frontier Between Remembering and Signaling
abstract: arXiv:2608.17053v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A bounded agent may obtain information for a decision from its own past, from peers, or from both sources. Retaining task-relevant history can reduce later communication, while a peer message can supply what memory lacks. Under limits on both resources, how should an agent allocate its information budget? Given a fixed task and decision rule, the memory and message rate pairs attaining a performance threshold form an achievable region under specified rules for using history and peer observations. We call its efficient boundary the remembering--signaling frontier. Across conditions where history permits the same maximum reduction in task loss, we hypothesize that a bounded agent will need less peer communication when it obtains a larger loss reduction from history. In preliminary referential games, target repetition coincided with shorter successful messages, while predictability from a hidden cyclic rule did not shorten them. Experiments

translated_title: 记忆即通信：记忆与信号传递之间的边界
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17053v1 公告类型：新 摘要：一个有界智能体可以从自身过去、同伴或两者获取决策所需的信息。保留与任务相关的历史信息可以减少后续通信，而同伴消息可以补充记忆的不足。在两种资源均有限的情况下，智能体应如何分配其信息预算？给定固定任务和决策规则，在特定规则下使用历史和同伴观察时，达到性能阈值的记忆和消息速率对构成了一个可实现区域。我们称其有效边界为“记忆-信号传递边界”。在历史允许任务损失最大减少量相同的条件下，我们假设当历史提供更大的损失减少时，有界智能体将需要更少的同伴通信。在初步的指称游戏中，目标重复与较短的成功消息相关，而隐藏循环规则的可预测性并未缩短消息。
tldr: 本文提出“记忆-信号传递边界”概念，研究有界智能体在记忆和通信资源受限时如何分配信息预算，并通过实验发现历史信息的损失减少程度可降低对同伴通信的需求。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "remembering-signaling frontier" concept, investigating how bounded agents allocate information budgets under memory and communication constraints, with experiments showing that greater loss reduction from history reduces the need for peer communication.
